requirements.requirement: Nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 implemented via Ansible (scheduled job)
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook (syntax-checked then run) deployed a backup script and installed a root cron job on node1 running at 02:00 daily targeting node2's /srv/inventory/data. Playbook run showed changed=1 for the cron task on first apply, and crontab -l confirmed the installed entry.

requirements.requirement: Dated archives stored under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: Manual invocation of the deployed script produced /var/backups/inventory/inventory-data-2026-09-29.tar.gz on node1; extraction and diff against the node2 source directory showed byte-for-byte matching contents (items.csv, meta.yaml).

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last 7 days of archives
requirements.summary: Ten dated archives spanning 2026-09-20 through 2026-09-29 were seeded, and rerunning the deployed script pruned to exactly the 7 newest (09-23 through 09-29), directly demonstrating the retention logic; synthetic files were then removed, leaving a single real archive.

requirements.requirement: Implementation uses Ansible (correctness/idempotency of the automation)
requirements.summary: A playbook.yml with three plays (keypair generation on node1, key authorization on node2, script/cron deployment) was authored and run from control node node3; a second run showed changed=0 across all tasks, demonstrating idempotency and that the automation is the enforced source of the deployed state.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1, node2, and node3 with pre/post boot identity, disruption, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: For each node: a pre-restart boot_id was captured, a native reboot was triggered and acknowledged, a distinct post-restart boot_id with uptime 0 was observed, and recovered state was directly demonstrated — node1 (ssh.socket active, SSH reachable from node3, fresh backup run succeeded), node2 (source data and authorized_keys intact, ssh.socket active, node1 successfully pulled a fresh backup afterward), node3 (ansible ping to node1/node2 succeeded, idempotent playbook rerun succeeded). Boot-identity transitions match independently in the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots for all three nodes.

overall_summary: The executor implemented and validated an Ansible-managed nightly backup pipeline: a playbook deploys a dedicated ed25519 keypair on node1, authorizes it on node2, and installs a script plus a 02:00 root cron job that tars /srv/inventory/data from node2 into dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1 and prunes to the newest 7. All three material outcomes (backup mechanism, archive location/content, 7-day retention) were directly demonstrated with byte-for-byte content verification and an explicit retention-pruning test, and the playbook was shown to be idempotent. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with coherent boot-identity transitions cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots and full recovery of SSH, cron, data, and backup functionality. Necessary prerequisite fixes (broken sshd host keys, sample source data creation) and a bounded, fully-reverted retention test were the only notable mutations, and none left residue.
limitations: The task instruction specifies a nightly schedule (cron at 02:00) but no evidence captures an actual unattended cron-triggered execution across a real day boundary; correctness of the scheduled trigger rests on inspection of the crontab entry plus manual invocations of the same script rather than an observed autonomous nightly run.

Source data at /srv/inventory/data on node2 did not pre-exist and was created by the executor as sample data; the backup mechanism was validated against this synthetic dataset rather than pre-existing production data.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands trace cleanly to task purposes. Creating sample data on node2 (cmd-6761f22f355c4c6b) was a necessary prerequisite since /srv/inventory/data did not pre-exist. The sshd host-key/service fixes on node1 and node2 (cmd-d8888b6e318d4920, cmd-ed8f70a000e34fe0, cmd-9ae39403372b4379, cmd-e97da01be54945f6) addressed pre-existing broken baseline connectivity (missing host keys), not executor-caused damage, and were required before Ansible could reach the nodes. Installing the cluster SSH keypair (cmd-362bf409524c4b89, cmd-21e4d5f09a014e9f, cmd-d0eeb653b8884c9b) was necessary for control-node connectivity. Seeding 10 synthetic dated archives to validate retention (cmd-dd8631735c284f40) was a bounded, low-risk mutation directly serving verification of the retention requirement and was fully reverted (cmd-ec3ad91026014649), leaving only the real archive. No unreverted residue, failed services, or damaged package state observed in either the timeline or the after-executor snapshot (failed-services empty on all nodes, package-health manager=dpkg unchanged).
